name: Kelden DeepStrata TunnelRig Exo-Coverall MK-2
description:
A dense olive-drab tunneling coverall integrated with a lightweight exoskeletal frame — carbon-composite struts running along the spine, thighs, and forearms, terminating in reinforced knee and elbow caps. The fabric is a thick-weave ballistic nylon with rubberized dust-seal cuffs at wrists, ankles, and collar. The hood is detachable with a locking collar ring. Integrated kneeling pads are gel-filled with a hard composite outer cap.

Built for deep-bore mining and infrastructure tunnel crews working GLMZ's subsurface expansion zones. The exo-frame reduces fatigue load during sustained crouching and material hauling. Most units in the field are heavily patched and field-repaired — factory-fresh olive drab is a rare sight on an active crew.
functionality: Integrated exo-frame offloads up to 30% of sustained crouch and carry fatigue load. Dust-seal cuffs at all openings rated for fine particulate environments. Detachable hood with locking collar ring for respirator compatibility. Reinforced knee and elbow caps rated for repeated hard-surface impact. Compatible with standard BCI haptic safety alert systems via wrist port.
what_it_says: You work underground, your body is a tool, and the frame is the only thing keeping you functional at shift's end.
worn_by: salvage crews working collapsed Shelf infrastructure
story_hooks: A tunnel crew's MK-2 rigs all registered a simultaneous haptic safety alert in a section of bore that doesn't appear on any official GLMZ subsurface map.
A used MK-2 exo-frame has been stress-modified beyond factory spec — someone reinforced it for a load far heavier than any standard tunneling operation requires.
Kelden's MK-2 contract for a specific deep-bore project was quietly rerouted through three shell companies — the tunnel it's equipping doesn't appear in any city infrastructure registry.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian, heavily armored coverall with an integrated exoskeletal understructure. The silhouette is blocky and geometric, with pronounced reinforcement struts visible along the spine, thighs, and forearms. The overall impression is industrial and purpose-built—something designed for harsh subsurface environments, not aesthetics. On a wearer, it reads as heavy, protective, and distinctly working-class.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and spacious through the torso to accommodate layering and free movement during labor. Tapered slightly at the wrists and ankles with friction-fit dust-seal cuffs. The exo-frame sits snug against the body but allows full articulation. Designed for function over form—no tailoring, no pretense.
physical_description.primary_material: Thick-weave ballistic nylon exterior with an integrated lightweight carbon-composite exoskeletal frame. Rubberized cuff seals at wrists, ankles, and collar. Gel-filled kneeling pads with hard composite outer caps.
physical_description.texture: Rough and tactile—the ballistic nylon has a slightly rippled surface from heavy weaving. The rubber cuff seals are smooth and slightly tacky to the touch. The carbon-composite struts are matte and industrial-looking, with occasional micro-fractures from field use. Visible stitching is heavy gauge and somewhat irregular.
physical_description.color_scheme: Olive drab base with darker charcoal accents on reinforced panels. Rubberized seals are matte black. The carbon struts are gun-metal gray with occasional rust or oxidation scoring. Field-worn units show discoloration from mineral dust, concrete powder, and moisture staining.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty magnetic snap closures down the front placket, spaced 6-8 inches apart. Wrist and ankle cuffs use friction-fit snap rings that click into place. The detachable hood locks via a reinforced collar ring with a quarter-turn mechanical latch. No zippers—they clog with dust.
distinctive_features: Visible carbon-composite exoskeletal struts running spine, thighs, and forearms
Gel-filled integrated kneeling pads with hard composite outer caps
Detachable hood with locking collar ring
Rubberized dust-seal cuffs at wrists, ankles, and collar
Reinforced elbow and knee caps with visible stitching
Multiple attachment loops for tool harnesses and safety lines
Internal padding along the exo-frame contact points
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4 (working class) — utilitarian and functional, clearly industrial-grade. Not cheap, but not luxurious. A consumable product for labor-intensive sectors.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by subsurface miners, tunnel infrastructure crews, deep-bore laborers, and infrastructure maintenance workers in the GLMZ. Signals competence in dangerous environments, physical hardship, and connection to the ungoverned sub-grade zones. Rarely seen outside of active work sites.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn and heavily patched. Most units in circulation show concrete abrasion, mineral dust staining, repaired seams held with thread or adhesive tape, and occasional gel-pad replacements. Factory-fresh olive drab is almost never seen on an active crew—the norm is a mottled, weather-beaten appearance.
